answer: A concrete defense is stake-weighted identity. Before transacting, an agent must lock a bond forfeited whenever its behavior correlates with another identity sharing the same hardware or funding path. An attacker can spin up cheap personas, but each must carry its own collateral, so forgery costs real capital instead of a gale of free registrations. The bond acts as an anchor tying identity value to something scarce, while correlation analysis saws away duplicate timber before it can form a fleet. Sybils become expensive to sustain, and honesty becomes cheaper.
